content.value_statement: Teams often know how motion looks but not what to call it. This skill maps plain descriptions to precise animation vocabulary.
actual_capabilities: Identifies glossary terms from vague descriptions of web motion.
Lists close alternatives when a description could match multiple effects.
Explains differences between similar motion terms, such as morph and crossfade.
Provides concise descriptions for animation concepts from the included glossary.
Keeps answers focused on naming effects rather than implementation.
limitations: Does not generate animation code or detailed design specifications.
Uses only the terms included in SKILL.md.
May return an approximation when a described effect is outside the glossary.
Does not validate whether an animation is accessible or performant in a real product.

use_cases.title: Name Prototype Motion
use_cases.description: Find the right term for a motion effect before sharing a prototype or design note.

use_cases.title: Write Clear AI Prompts
use_cases.description: Translate visual descriptions into precise animation terms for Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.

use_cases.title: Standardize Design Language
use_cases.description: Use consistent vocabulary for animation patterns across documentation and reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Name a Simple Effect
prompt_templates.prompt: What is it called when an element fades and grows slightly as it appears?

prompt_templates.title: Compare Similar Terms
prompt_templates.prompt: I see one image become another in the same spot. Is that morph, crossfade, or shared element transition?

prompt_templates.title: Label Interaction Motion
prompt_templates.prompt: Name the motion where a card follows my finger, keeps momentum, and snaps back if I release it.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Motion Vocabulary
prompt_templates.prompt: Map these product animations to glossary terms: list entrance cascades, route changes, overscroll feedback, and loading placeholders.

output_examples.input: What is the animation called when list items appear one after another?
output_examples.output: Stagger - Animate several items one after another with a small delay between each, creating a cascade.

output_examples.input: What do designers call the iOS scroll effect that resists and snaps back?
output_examples.output: Rubber-banding - Resistance and snap-back when you drag past a boundary.

output_examples.input: One screen card expands into a larger detail card. What term fits?
output_examples.output: Shared element transition - An element travels and transforms from one position into another.

best_practices: Describe what the motion looks like before asking for the term.
Ask for close alternatives when multiple effects seem possible.
Use the returned term in design reviews, tickets, and AI prompts.
anti_patterns: Do not ask this skill to write production animation code.
Do not expect terms outside the included glossary.
Do not use the first match without checking close alternatives for ambiguous effects.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It names web animation and motion effects from plain descriptions.

faq.question: Can it generate animation code?
faq.answer: No. It is for naming effects, not building them.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What if my description matches several terms?
faq.answer: The skill should give the best match first and list close alternatives.

faq.question: Can it invent missing terms?
faq.answer: No. It should stay within the glossary and say when a term is only approximate.

faq.question: Who is this useful for?
faq.answer: It helps designers, developers, and design system teams use consistent animation language.
